because the file is ~1450 lines; every part is idempotent.

ONE PREDICTION WAS WRONG, AND IT MATTERED

  Predicted: "invoice.prepared_by_user_id null = the first ops admin, which is
  Lone."
  Actual:    it resolved to france@keywealth.co.bw.

  _handover_owner() falls back to the first admin BY EMAIL. In the local
  fixture Lone is the only admin, so the fallback looked like "Lone". On live
  there are five admins and france@ sorts before lone@ alphabetically.

  So the default would have put Lone's invoice pack in France's name -- and
  France is precisely the person who LOSES ops-admin capability when M3 lands.
  The deploy note always said to set this key explicitly; the fallback was
  never meant to be relied on.

  FIXED at apply time:
    update threshold_config
       set value = to_jsonb('<lone-user-id>'::text)
     where key = 'invoice.prepared_by_user_id';

    invoice.prepared_by_user_id : a9e42be3-ed16-4597-8f49-861069becb42
    resolves to                 : lone@keywellness.co.bw

  This is what the baseline-and-prediction rule is for. A local green said the
  fallback was fine; only the live diff showed it was not.

STILL TRUE AFTER M4
  No contract, no rate and no handover exists. The first pack appears on the
  25th of the first month a retainer contract exists. Lone marks it handed
  over herself, from the SQL editor, until M7 gives her a button.
